# Testament of Naphtali — 8
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** The copy of the testament of Naphtali, which he ordained at the time of his death in the hundred and thirty-second year of his life. **2** When his sons were gathered together in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, while still in good health, he made them a feast and drank wine. **3** And after he was awake in the morning he said to them: I am dying. And they believed him not. **4** And as he blessed the Lord, he grew strong and said that after yesterday's feast he would die. **5** And he began then to say: Hear me, my children, hear Naphtali your father, the things which I command you. **6** For I have seen in all my life that the judgment of God is true and righteous.

**2** I was born from Bilhah; and because Rachel dealt cunningly, and gave Bilhah in place of herself to Jacob, and she conceived and bore me upon Rachel's knees, therefore she called my name Naphtali. **2** For Rachel loved me very much, because I was born upon her lap; and when I was still tender she would kiss me, saying: May I have a brother of thine from mine own womb, like unto thee. **3** Whence also Joseph was like unto me in all things, according to the prayers of Rachel. **4** Now my mother was Bilhah, daughter of Rotheus the brother of Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, who was born on one and the same day with Rachel. **5** And Rotheus was of the family of Abraham, a Chaldean, God-fearing, free-born and noble; and he was taken captive and bought by Laban; and he gave him Euna his handmaid to wife, and she bore Bilhah and Zilpah to him.

**3** And God made all things good in their order: the five senses in the head, and He added thereunto the neck, the hair also for comeliness and glory, the heart moreover for understanding, the belly for excretion, the windpipe for health, the liver for wrath, the gall for bitterness, the spleen for laughter, the reins for prudence, the loins for power, the backbone for fortitude. **2** So then understand all things in order, and know that as the Lord made the body a type of the spirit, so also He made the spirit after the type of the body, fitting every work of the Most High, that the body be perfect in its own works. **3** For in the like manner as the senses of the body work together with each other, so also do the senses of the soul work one with another.

**4** Therefore understand all things in order, my children, and give diligence in all your doings to be orderly and proper before all men; and whatsoever the Lord commands in the order of His will, do ye in due order, and nothing out of season. **2** For if thou tell the sun to go faster, it will not obey thee; neither will it cease shining if thou command it; for it abideth in the order God created it. **3** And so the moon and the stars do not change their order. **4** So also ye: do not change the law of God in the disorderliness of your doings.

**5** And I saw that in Jacob's sons there was the fulfilment of all these things. **2** For in Levi and Judah were the true-born priests and kings; and all the Gentiles shall be brought low, through them; and Israel shall be glorified through them. **3** For the Lord took them, and so shall it be unto the end, and there is hope for all who look to him.

**6** And I saw a vision on the Mount of Olives, that the sun and the moon stood still, and Isaac our father was beneath the olive tree, praying for us; and we his sons went round about him. **2** And behold, there came a bull, having two great horns, and an eagle's wings upon his back; and we wished to seize him, but could not. **3** And Joseph fled before us and mounted on the bull; and Jacob our father ran and seized the bull; and the bull was caught, and Jacob rejoiced over him. **4** And I saw in my sleep that twelve deer were feeding; and nine of them were divided and scattered, and the three also: and I saw that from Judah was born a virgin wearing a linen garment, and from her went forth a Lamb, without spot; and on his left hand there was as it were a lion, and all the beasts rushed against him, and the Lamb overcame them and destroyed them and trod them under foot. **5** And on account of him the angels and men rejoiced, and all the land. **6** And these things shall come to pass in their season in the last days.

**7** Do ye therefore, my children, also keep the law of God, and acquire simplicity, and walk in guilelessness, not playing the busybody with the business of your neighbour, but love the Lord and your neighbour. **2** For these things and all the commandments of the Lord are sufficient for you; for ye know that to whatever degree a man walketh in simplicity before God, so much doth God bless him. **3** And after he had said these things, he charged them to carry his bones up to Hebron and bury them there with his fathers; and while he was eating and drinking in much gladness, he covered his face and died.

---
*End of Testament of Naphtali*
